1. Define archaeology. Trace the evolution of archacology as a discipline and analyse different archaeological theories.
2.. Discuss the role of Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in archaeological research and development.
3. How has the integration of modern scientific tools and digital technologies changed traditional archaeological survey methods ?
4. Explain the various methods of archaeological excavations. Underline their relative importance.
Describe the various techniques and typology of stone tools of-prehistoric period.
6. "Pottery is often called the alphabet of archaeology". Elaborate this statement in the light of various analytical approaches and technological aspects of ceramic manufacture.
Based on your observations at any site/museum, write a report on significant objects and explain why they are important to our understanding of the past.
8. Write short notes on any two of the following :
(a) Aims and scope of Archaeology
(b) Scientific dating methods
(c) Settlement archaeology
(d) . Classification of Archaeological objects.

1.. How does the urban-rural fringe illustrate and affect the broader phenomenon of urbanisation ? Discuss.
(2) What do you mean by the term Urbanisation ? What are the various •
approaches used for studying urbanisation?..
Critically assess the role of town planning, trade network, and craft specialisation as the crucial features in the rise of Harappan urbanisation.
4. Evaluate the significance of trade and religion as driving forces behind the urbanisation process in early India. Illustrate your answer with specific reference to the city of Kanchipuram.
Analyse the various causes that led to Agra becoming the pre-eminent imperial city of Medieval India.
6., How far do you agree that Hampi exemplifies the synthesis of power, piety, and commerce during the Vijayanagar Empire ?
7. How far did the colonial opium trade have a bearing on the urban structural development of colonial Bombay?
8. With respect to colonial Calcutta in the late nineteenth and twentieth centuries, describe how the British planned the development of a modern urban space.
